top_news.title: US delegation expected in Doha for direct Iran talks after reported breakthrough: Reports
top_news.summary: An American delegation is expected to join Iranian officials for direct talks in Doha following a reported breakthrough in indirect negotiations between Washington and Tehran, The Times of Israel reported, citing the Qatari newspaper Al-Araby Al-Jadeed. According to the report, citing sources close to mediation efforts led by Qatar and Pakistan, the two sides have reached an understanding on preliminary measures concerning Iran's nuclear programme, navigation through the Strait of Hormuz and financial incentives for Tehran. China and Russia are also reportedly expected to serve as guarantors of any agreement. The reported progress follows more than 12 hours of discussionsbetweenQatari mediators and Iranian officials in Tehran on Friday, aimed at restarting direct negotiations between Washington and Tehran and preventing a renewed outbreak of war, according to Axios. Citing diplomatic sources, Axios reported that the discussions were held amid growing concerns over a possible US military operation against Iran following the November 3 midterm elections. The talks are set to continue in Doha on Saturday. A diplomatic source told Axios that Qatari mediators remained in regular contact with the White House during Friday's discussions. "There was positive progress. Talks are still ongoing in an effort to unlock a deal between the US and Iran," the source said. Qatar is pushing both sides to agree on a series of reciprocal steps that could be implemented over a few days, paving the way for the resumption of direct negotiations on Iran's nuclear programme and other issues. However, differences over the conditions for restarting negotiations have continued to complicate the diplomatic efforts. According to a US official cited by Axios, the Trump administration wants Iran to make nuclear concessions as a condition for resuming talks, while Tehran has demanded that Washington first lift its naval blockade, release frozen funds and allow it to sell oil. Qatari mediators are also seeking to persuade Iran to allow United Nations inspectors to visit its bombed nuclear sites as a confidence-building measure, in return for possible sanctions relief from Washington. Meanwhile, a preliminary draft framework for US-Iran negotiations proposes transferring Iran's highly enriched uranium stockpile to an agreed third country or reducing its enrichment level, while reopening the Strait of Hormuz to international maritime traffic within seven days of an initial understanding, Al Arabiya English reported. According to Al Arabiya English, which exclusively obtained the draft's key points, China could potentially act as a guarantor for the implementation and sustainability of any agreement. The framework also proposes holding direct US-Iran negotiations in Doha instead of Istanbul. Under the proposed arrangement, Iran's measures on its nuclear programme and maritime security would be matched by US steps to ease sanctions, blockades and economic restrictions. An independent verification mechanism would assess compliance before each phase of implementation, ensuring that neither side makes substantial concessions without corresponding, independently verifiable commitments. The draft also proposes a dispute-resolution mechanism involving mediators and guarantor parties to address delays or violations and prevent renewed military escalation, according to the news platform. Meanwhile, divisions reportedly persist within US President Donald Trump's administration over the next course of action. US Secretary of War Pete Hegseth and Secretary of State Marco Rubio are highly sceptical about the possibility of reaching a nuclear agreement with the current Iranian regime and favour further weakening it, including through additional strikes, a US official told Axios. In contrast, Vice President JD Vance and Trump's envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are in favour of resuming negotiations. Trump, however, remains sceptical about whether Tehran would accept an agreement meeting his expectations. "There are talks. They want to talk. They keep talking. ...We have time, frankly. It's a war, but it is not a typical war," Trump told reporters on Friday. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, who is leading the administration's economic pressure campaign, dubbed "Operation Economic Outcast", is also among the senior officials urging Trump to allow the initiative to continue rather than rush into renewed military action, Axios reported. Regional countries, including Egypt, Turkey, Iraq, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia, have also been pressing Iran to resume negotiations before the US midterm elections, according to a regional source cited by Axios. The diplomatic push comes amid concerns that a renewed conflict could trigger widespread destruction across Iran and the Gulf region, further worsening the global energy crisis. Iran has threatened to retaliate against any US strikes on its energy infrastructure by targeting oil and gas facilities in Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Kuwait and Bahrain. According to Axios, any renewed US military operation against Iran would be conducted jointly with Israel, with Tehran likely to respond through missile strikes. Hezbollah could also launch attacks against Israel. Meanwhile, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is reportedly lobbying Trump to launch a joint military operation against Iran immediately after the US midterm elections, adding to the uncertainty surrounding the diplomatic efforts. (ANI)

top_news.title: FATF countries agree on global action against evolving financial crime threats; remove Bulgaria, Ivory Coast, Congo and Monaco from
top_news.summary: The inaugural Financial Action Task Force (FATF) Plenary meeting under the UK Presidency of Giles Thomson concluded in Paris, with countries agreeing on global action to tackle evolving financial crime threats, including the rising threat posed by virtual assets, fraud and scam compounds. According to a statement of outcomes by FATF member countries, in response to the FATF Ministerial Declaration of April 2026, the Plenary agreed to significantly accelerate the effective implementation of the FATF Standards on virtual assets (VAs) in jurisdictions with materially important VA activity. The Plenary recognised the need to urgently strengthen countries' defences against the rising threat posed by the misuse of virtual assets for money laundering, terrorist financing and proliferation financing. The Plenary approved a report that elevates the fight against fraud and scam compounds as a global priority, providing a strong basis for the FATF and its Global Network to intensify efforts to identify, disrupt and deprive the criminal networks behind these operations of their illicit profits. This is the first output in the FATF's Roadmap on combatting fraud under the UK Presidency, and will be followed by a wider study and recommendations for how the FATF toolkit can be used to combat fraud more broadly. The FATF agreed to remove Bulgaria, Cote d'Ivoire, the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Monaco from its list of jurisdictions under increased monitoring following successful on-site visits, and the FATF updated its statements on jurisdictions under increased monitoring and jurisdictions subject to a call for action. The jurisdictions are actively working with the FATF and the Global Network to address the strategic deficiencies in their regimes to counter money laundering, terrorist financing and proliferation financing. When the FATF places a jurisdiction under increased monitoring, it means the jurisdiction has committed to implement an Action Plan to swiftly resolve the identified strategic deficiencies within agreed timeframes. Following successful on-site visits, the Plenary noted the positive progress in addressing strategic anti-money laundering and countering the financing of terrorism and proliferation financing (AML/CFT/CPF) deficiencies identified during their mutual evaluations. The jurisdictions have completed their Action Plans within agreed timeframes and will no longer be subject to the FATF's increased monitoring process. The jurisdictions will continue working with their relevant FATF-Style Regional Bodies (FSRBs), GIABA (Cote d'Ivoire), GABAC and ESAAMLG (Democratic Republic of Congo) and MONEYVAL (Bulgaria, Monaco), to sustain improvements in their AML/CFT/CPF systems. In its statement on Vietnam, the FATF expressed significant concern with its pace of progress. The FATF will consider next steps if Vietnam does not make tangible improvements to rectify its strategic deficiencies by the next Plenary meeting. The FATF has updated its public statements on two of the high-risk jurisdictions (Black List), Myanmar and Iran, reinforcing its call on Myanmar to address the extensive fraud and scam activities emanating from the country, and the call on Iran to criminalise terrorist financing and establish a targeted financial sanctions regime in line with the FATF Standards. And the Plenary agreed to introduce tailored assessments for low-capacity countries, enabling a more risk-based prioritisation of high-impact reforms. With criminal networks increasingly abusing virtual assets (VAs) for a range of illicit purposes, including fraud, scams, sanctions evasion, money laundering, terrorism financing, and proliferation financing, the Plenary agreed to launch a new targeted review and accelerated follow-up processes to support jurisdictions in addressing gaps in implementation of the FATF Standards on VAs and virtual asset service providers (VASPs) more rapidly. The targeted review will be based on objective criteria and will focus on jurisdictions with materially important VA sectors on the basis of their assessment status. The results will be published in June and October 2027. The FATF will work closely with relevant jurisdictions to support implementation efforts in this sector, including through ongoing engagement, training, and capacity-building initiatives. According to the statement, the Plenary approved a new report, to be published next week, which examines the end-to-end illicit financial flows linked to scam compounds, which are among the most rapidly expanding forms of organised crime globally, and contribute significantly to rising levels of fraud and associated proceeds. By drawing on operational insights from across the FATF Global Network, the report will help authorities to dismantle the increasingly integrated criminal business models and professionalised crime-as-a-service economy that sustain scam compounds around the world. The report will inform the next phase of the FATF's work on fraud as members consider how to further mobilise the Task Force's full set of capabilities to combat fraud in line with the FATF Ministerial Declaration of April 2026. The Plenary adopted reports of Mexico and the United States under the new round of mutual evaluations. These reports assessed the effectiveness of the countries' measures to combat money laundering, terrorist financing and proliferation financing, and compliance with the FATF Recommendations. The reports will be published in December 2026, following a quality and consistency review. Under the new round of mutual evaluations, countries receive a time-bound Roadmap of Key Recommended Actions required within three years to strengthen the effectiveness of their defences against illicit finance. The FATF will host a Learning and Development Forum in Dallas, Texas, on December 1 and 2, focused on alignment on risk assessment and understanding risk in support of a more risk-based prioritisation of resources, a shift in financial crime risk management and supervisory culture, and greater effectiveness. This Forum will convene supervisors, financial intelligence units, law enforcement, financial institutions and non-financial institutions from across the world to develop a concrete policy statement - to be published shortly afterwards - to support a reinterpretation of how the risk-based approach should be implemented in practice. As per the statement, the FATF has agreed to continue the suspension of membership for Russia. The delegates from across the FATF's Global Network of more than 200 jurisdictions and observers gathered in Paris from October 28 to 30. By invitation of the FATF President, representatives of Barbados, Namibia and Thailand participated under their own flags for the first time through the FATF Guest Initiative, which enhances the FATF's global response to fighting financial crime, the statement read. top_news.title: Himachal: CM Sukhu, Congress leaders pay tribute to Indira Gandhi; remember Sardar Patel on birth anniversary
top_news.summary: Himachal Pradesh Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu, Deputy Chief Minister Mukesh Agnihotri and senior Congress leaders on Saturday paid floral tributes to former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi on her death anniversary and remembered Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel on his birth anniversary, highlighting their contributions to the country's unity, democratic institutions and nation-building. The Chief Minister also administered the oath on the occasion, while leaders and party workers gathered to pay homage to the two prominent personalities. Former Himachal Pradesh Congress Committee president Pratibha Singh, Health Minister Col (Retd) Dhaniram Shandil, Deputy Chief Minister Mukesh Agnihotri, members of the Congress Seva Dal, and Shimla Mayor and Deputy Mayor paid floral tributes at the statue of Indira Gandhi in the state capital. Speaking to reporters, Pratibha Singh said the country would always remain grateful to Indira Gandhi for her contribution and the policies implemented during her tenure as Prime Minister. Indira Gandhi ji, our country's Prime Minister, today we all remember her and pay our heartfelt tribute. The work she did during her tenure benefited millions of people, including the youth, and we will always remain grateful to her, she said. She said the occasion was also an opportunity to remember Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel and convey the message and contributions of both leaders to the younger generation. We will try to follow their path so that the work they did and their message reach our youth. The youth should know how the leaders of that generation guided the country and took it forward, Pratibha Singh said. She said the Congress leaders had also taken a pledge to work for the country's betterment while taking the youth along. Health Minister Col (Retd) Dhaniram Shandil said Indira Gandhi's leadership during the 1971 war and her decision-making ability had strengthened the morale of the armed forces. Recalling her visit to the frontline during the war, he said the former Prime Minister demonstrated courage by visiting areas where the Army was deployed.She was an Iron Lady. The way she raised the morale of our soldiers and took decisions during difficult circumstances will always be remembered, Shandil said. He said Indira Gandhi had also taken several important decisions concerning the country's economic and social development. Referring to her 20-point programme and initiatives related to women, he said her contribution had provided direction to the country and needed to be communicated to the younger generation. Shandil also paid tribute to Sardar Patel, describing him as a courageous leader who played a crucial role in integrating more than 600 princely states into the Indian Union. Remembering these great personalities and making the younger generation aware of their contributions is very important, he said. Deputy Chief Minister Mukesh Agnihotri said October 31 was significant for the country as it marked the death anniversary of Indira Gandhi and the birth anniversary of Sardar Patel. He said Indira Gandhi had established India's position internationally through her leadership during the 1971 war and the creation of Bangladesh. Indira Gandhi ji made India respected across the world. During the 1971 war, she played a decisive role in the liberation of Bangladesh and the surrender of Pakistani forces, Agnihotri said. He said her contribution was particularly significant for Himachal Pradesh, as she played an important role in the state's emergence as a separate state. Indira Gandhi ji is important for Himachal because she gave the state its identity as a separate state. She listened to the voice of the people of the hills and ensured that Himachal Pradesh became a separate state, he said. Agnihotri said the people of Himachal would always remain grateful to her for the decision. He also recalled Sardar Patel's contribution to national integration, saying the integration of princely states had laid the foundation for a united India. Sardar Patel was an Iron Man. His decisions and his role in integrating the princely states into the country will always be remembered, he said. Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu described Indira Gandhi as a courageous and decisive leader whose decisions had shaped the country's history.Indira Gandhi was a personality who never feared, who was courageous and always had the ability to take decisions. One of her decisions changed the course of Pakistan, Sukhu said. He said her leadership during the 1971 war had resulted in the liberation of Bangladesh and demonstrated her commitment to India's unity and integrity. Sukhu also recalled her decisions on land ceiling, abolition of privy purses and nationalisation of banks, saying these had shaped the country's economic and social policies. She took important decisions for the unity and integrity of the country and sacrificed her life for the nation, he said. The Chief Minister said the Congress had played a significant role in strengthening democratic institutions and protecting the Constitution after Independence. He said the Constitution drafted under the leadership of Dr B R Ambedkar had provided citizens with the right to vote and participate in democracy. Through the same Constitution and the same democratic system, Prime Minister Narendra Modi also came to power. The right to vote is the foundation of our democracy, and it is important that this right is protected, Sukhu said. He said Sardar Patel's contribution to the integration of princely states, including Jammu and Kashmir and Hyderabad, had earned him the title of Iron Man. The leaders said the occasion was an opportunity to remember the contributions of both personalities and inspire the younger generation to work towards national unity, democratic values and the country's development. articles.title: US delegation expected in Doha for direct Iran talks after reported breakthrough: Reports
articles.summary: An American delegation is expected to join Iranian officials for direct talks in Doha following a reported breakthrough in indirect negotiations between Washington and Tehran, The Times of Israel reported, citing the Qatari newspaper Al-Araby Al-Jadeed. According to the report, citing sources close to mediation efforts led by Qatar and Pakistan, the two sides have reached an understanding on preliminary measures concerning Iran's nuclear programme, navigation through the Strait of Hormuz and financial incentives for Tehran. China and Russia are also reportedly expected to serve as guarantors of any agreement. The reported progress follows more than 12 hours of discussionsbetweenQatari mediators and Iranian officials in Tehran on Friday, aimed at restarting direct negotiations between Washington and Tehran and preventing a renewed outbreak of war, according to Axios. Citing diplomatic sources, Axios reported that the discussions were held amid growing concerns over a possible US military operation against Iran following the November 3 midterm elections. The talks are set to continue in Doha on Saturday. A diplomatic source told Axios that Qatari mediators remained in regular contact with the White House during Friday's discussions. "There was positive progress. Talks are still ongoing in an effort to unlock a deal between the US and Iran," the source said. Qatar is pushing both sides to agree on a series of reciprocal steps that could be implemented over a few days, paving the way for the resumption of direct negotiations on Iran's nuclear programme and other issues. However, differences over the conditions for restarting negotiations have continued to complicate the diplomatic efforts. According to a US official cited by Axios, the Trump administration wants Iran to make nuclear concessions as a condition for resuming talks, while Tehran has demanded that Washington first lift its naval blockade, release frozen funds and allow it to sell oil. Qatari mediators are also seeking to persuade Iran to allow United Nations inspectors to visit its bombed nuclear sites as a confidence-building measure, in return for possible sanctions relief from Washington. Meanwhile, a preliminary draft framework for US-Iran negotiations proposes transferring Iran's highly enriched uranium stockpile to an agreed third country or reducing its enrichment level, while reopening the Strait of Hormuz to international maritime traffic within seven days of an initial understanding, Al Arabiya English reported. According to Al Arabiya English, which exclusively obtained the draft's key points, China could potentially act as a guarantor for the implementation and sustainability of any agreement. The framework also proposes holding direct US-Iran negotiations in Doha instead of Istanbul. Under the proposed arrangement, Iran's measures on its nuclear programme and maritime security would be matched by US steps to ease sanctions, blockades and economic restrictions. An independent verification mechanism would assess compliance before each phase of implementation, ensuring that neither side makes substantial concessions without corresponding, independently verifiable commitments. The draft also proposes a dispute-resolution mechanism involving mediators and guarantor parties to address delays or violations and prevent renewed military escalation, according to the news platform. Meanwhile, divisions reportedly persist within US President Donald Trump's administration over the next course of action. US Secretary of War Pete Hegseth and Secretary of State Marco Rubio are highly sceptical about the possibility of reaching a nuclear agreement with the current Iranian regime and favour further weakening it, including through additional strikes, a US official told Axios. In contrast, Vice President JD Vance and Trump's envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are in favour of resuming negotiations. Trump, however, remains sceptical about whether Tehran would accept an agreement meeting his expectations. "There are talks. They want to talk. They keep talking. ...We have time, frankly. It's a war, but it is not a typical war," Trump told reporters on Friday. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, who is leading the administration's economic pressure campaign, dubbed "Operation Economic Outcast", is also among the senior officials urging Trump to allow the initiative to continue rather than rush into renewed military action, Axios reported. Regional countries, including Egypt, Turkey, Iraq, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia, have also been pressing Iran to resume negotiations before the US midterm elections, according to a regional source cited by Axios. The diplomatic push comes amid concerns that a renewed conflict could trigger widespread destruction across Iran and the Gulf region, further worsening the global energy crisis. Iran has threatened to retaliate against any US strikes on its energy infrastructure by targeting oil and gas facilities in Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Kuwait and Bahrain. According to Axios, any renewed US military operation against Iran would be conducted jointly with Israel, with Tehran likely to respond through missile strikes. Hezbollah could also launch attacks against Israel. Meanwhile, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is reportedly lobbying Trump to launch a joint military operation against Iran immediately after the US midterm elections, adding to the uncertainty surrounding the diplomatic efforts. (ANI)

articles.title: FATF countries agree on global action against evolving financial crime threats; remove Bulgaria, Ivory Coast, Congo and Monaco from
articles.summary: The inaugural Financial Action Task Force (FATF) Plenary meeting under the UK Presidency of Giles Thomson concluded in Paris, with countries agreeing on global action to tackle evolving financial crime threats, including the rising threat posed by virtual assets, fraud and scam compounds. According to a statement of outcomes by FATF member countries, in response to the FATF Ministerial Declaration of April 2026, the Plenary agreed to significantly accelerate the effective implementation of the FATF Standards on virtual assets (VAs) in jurisdictions with materially important VA activity. The Plenary recognised the need to urgently strengthen countries' defences against the rising threat posed by the misuse of virtual assets for money laundering, terrorist financing and proliferation financing. The Plenary approved a report that elevates the fight against fraud and scam compounds as a global priority, providing a strong basis for the FATF and its Global Network to intensify efforts to identify, disrupt and deprive the criminal networks behind these operations of their illicit profits. This is the first output in the FATF's Roadmap on combatting fraud under the UK Presidency, and will be followed by a wider study and recommendations for how the FATF toolkit can be used to combat fraud more broadly. The FATF agreed to remove Bulgaria, Cote d'Ivoire, the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Monaco from its list of jurisdictions under increased monitoring following successful on-site visits, and the FATF updated its statements on jurisdictions under increased monitoring and jurisdictions subject to a call for action. The jurisdictions are actively working with the FATF and the Global Network to address the strategic deficiencies in their regimes to counter money laundering, terrorist financing and proliferation financing. When the FATF places a jurisdiction under increased monitoring, it means the jurisdiction has committed to implement an Action Plan to swiftly resolve the identified strategic deficiencies within agreed timeframes. Following successful on-site visits, the Plenary noted the positive progress in addressing strategic anti-money laundering and countering the financing of terrorism and proliferation financing (AML/CFT/CPF) deficiencies identified during their mutual evaluations. The jurisdictions have completed their Action Plans within agreed timeframes and will no longer be subject to the FATF's increased monitoring process. The jurisdictions will continue working with their relevant FATF-Style Regional Bodies (FSRBs), GIABA (Cote d'Ivoire), GABAC and ESAAMLG (Democratic Republic of Congo) and MONEYVAL (Bulgaria, Monaco), to sustain improvements in their AML/CFT/CPF systems. In its statement on Vietnam, the FATF expressed significant concern with its pace of progress. The FATF will consider next steps if Vietnam does not make tangible improvements to rectify its strategic deficiencies by the next Plenary meeting. The FATF has updated its public statements on two of the high-risk jurisdictions (Black List), Myanmar and Iran, reinforcing its call on Myanmar to address the extensive fraud and scam activities emanating from the country, and the call on Iran to criminalise terrorist financing and establish a targeted financial sanctions regime in line with the FATF Standards. And the Plenary agreed to introduce tailored assessments for low-capacity countries, enabling a more risk-based prioritisation of high-impact reforms. With criminal networks increasingly abusing virtual assets (VAs) for a range of illicit purposes, including fraud, scams, sanctions evasion, money laundering, terrorism financing, and proliferation financing, the Plenary agreed to launch a new targeted review and accelerated follow-up processes to support jurisdictions in addressing gaps in implementation of the FATF Standards on VAs and virtual asset service providers (VASPs) more rapidly. The targeted review will be based on objective criteria and will focus on jurisdictions with materially important VA sectors on the basis of their assessment status. The results will be published in June and October 2027. The FATF will work closely with relevant jurisdictions to support implementation efforts in this sector, including through ongoing engagement, training, and capacity-building initiatives. According to the statement, the Plenary approved a new report, to be published next week, which examines the end-to-end illicit financial flows linked to scam compounds, which are among the most rapidly expanding forms of organised crime globally, and contribute significantly to rising levels of fraud and associated proceeds. By drawing on operational insights from across the FATF Global Network, the report will help authorities to dismantle the increasingly integrated criminal business models and professionalised crime-as-a-service economy that sustain scam compounds around the world. The report will inform the next phase of the FATF's work on fraud as members consider how to further mobilise the Task Force's full set of capabilities to combat fraud in line with the FATF Ministerial Declaration of April 2026. The Plenary adopted reports of Mexico and the United States under the new round of mutual evaluations. These reports assessed the effectiveness of the countries' measures to combat money laundering, terrorist financing and proliferation financing, and compliance with the FATF Recommendations. The reports will be published in December 2026, following a quality and consistency review. Under the new round of mutual evaluations, countries receive a time-bound Roadmap of Key Recommended Actions required within three years to strengthen the effectiveness of their defences against illicit finance. The FATF will host a Learning and Development Forum in Dallas, Texas, on December 1 and 2, focused on alignment on risk assessment and understanding risk in support of a more risk-based prioritisation of resources, a shift in financial crime risk management and supervisory culture, and greater effectiveness. This Forum will convene supervisors, financial intelligence units, law enforcement, financial institutions and non-financial institutions from across the world to develop a concrete policy statement - to be published shortly afterwards - to support a reinterpretation of how the risk-based approach should be implemented in practice. As per the statement, the FATF has agreed to continue the suspension of membership for Russia. The delegates from across the FATF's Global Network of more than 200 jurisdictions and observers gathered in Paris from October 28 to 30. By invitation of the FATF President, representatives of Barbados, Namibia and Thailand participated under their own flags for the first time through the FATF Guest Initiative, which enhances the FATF's global response to fighting financial crime, the statement read. articles.title: Himachal: CM Sukhu, Congress leaders pay tribute to Indira Gandhi; remember Sardar Patel on birth anniversary
articles.summary: Himachal Pradesh Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu, Deputy Chief Minister Mukesh Agnihotri and senior Congress leaders on Saturday paid floral tributes to former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi on her death anniversary and remembered Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel on his birth anniversary, highlighting their contributions to the country's unity, democratic institutions and nation-building. The Chief Minister also administered the oath on the occasion, while leaders and party workers gathered to pay homage to the two prominent personalities. Former Himachal Pradesh Congress Committee president Pratibha Singh, Health Minister Col (Retd) Dhaniram Shandil, Deputy Chief Minister Mukesh Agnihotri, members of the Congress Seva Dal, and Shimla Mayor and Deputy Mayor paid floral tributes at the statue of Indira Gandhi in the state capital. Speaking to reporters, Pratibha Singh said the country would always remain grateful to Indira Gandhi for her contribution and the policies implemented during her tenure as Prime Minister. Indira Gandhi ji, our country's Prime Minister, today we all remember her and pay our heartfelt tribute. The work she did during her tenure benefited millions of people, including the youth, and we will always remain grateful to her, she said. She said the occasion was also an opportunity to remember Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel and convey the message and contributions of both leaders to the younger generation. We will try to follow their path so that the work they did and their message reach our youth. The youth should know how the leaders of that generation guided the country and took it forward, Pratibha Singh said. She said the Congress leaders had also taken a pledge to work for the country's betterment while taking the youth along. Health Minister Col (Retd) Dhaniram Shandil said Indira Gandhi's leadership during the 1971 war and her decision-making ability had strengthened the morale of the armed forces. Recalling her visit to the frontline during the war, he said the former Prime Minister demonstrated courage by visiting areas where the Army was deployed.She was an Iron Lady. The way she raised the morale of our soldiers and took decisions during difficult circumstances will always be remembered, Shandil said. He said Indira Gandhi had also taken several important decisions concerning the country's economic and social development. Referring to her 20-point programme and initiatives related to women, he said her contribution had provided direction to the country and needed to be communicated to the younger generation. Shandil also paid tribute to Sardar Patel, describing him as a courageous leader who played a crucial role in integrating more than 600 princely states into the Indian Union. Remembering these great personalities and making the younger generation aware of their contributions is very important, he said. Deputy Chief Minister Mukesh Agnihotri said October 31 was significant for the country as it marked the death anniversary of Indira Gandhi and the birth anniversary of Sardar Patel. He said Indira Gandhi had established India's position internationally through her leadership during the 1971 war and the creation of Bangladesh. Indira Gandhi ji made India respected across the world. During the 1971 war, she played a decisive role in the liberation of Bangladesh and the surrender of Pakistani forces, Agnihotri said. He said her contribution was particularly significant for Himachal Pradesh, as she played an important role in the state's emergence as a separate state. Indira Gandhi ji is important for Himachal because she gave the state its identity as a separate state. She listened to the voice of the people of the hills and ensured that Himachal Pradesh became a separate state, he said. Agnihotri said the people of Himachal would always remain grateful to her for the decision. He also recalled Sardar Patel's contribution to national integration, saying the integration of princely states had laid the foundation for a united India. Sardar Patel was an Iron Man. His decisions and his role in integrating the princely states into the country will always be remembered, he said. Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu described Indira Gandhi as a courageous and decisive leader whose decisions had shaped the country's history.Indira Gandhi was a personality who never feared, who was courageous and always had the ability to take decisions. One of her decisions changed the course of Pakistan, Sukhu said. He said her leadership during the 1971 war had resulted in the liberation of Bangladesh and demonstrated her commitment to India's unity and integrity. Sukhu also recalled her decisions on land ceiling, abolition of privy purses and nationalisation of banks, saying these had shaped the country's economic and social policies. She took important decisions for the unity and integrity of the country and sacrificed her life for the nation, he said. The Chief Minister said the Congress had played a significant role in strengthening democratic institutions and protecting the Constitution after Independence. He said the Constitution drafted under the leadership of Dr B R Ambedkar had provided citizens with the right to vote and participate in democracy. Through the same Constitution and the same democratic system, Prime Minister Narendra Modi also came to power. The right to vote is the foundation of our democracy, and it is important that this right is protected, Sukhu said. He said Sardar Patel's contribution to the integration of princely states, including Jammu and Kashmir and Hyderabad, had earned him the title of Iron Man. The leaders said the occasion was an opportunity to remember the contributions of both personalities and inspire the younger generation to work towards national unity, democratic values and the country's development. articles.title: Column: What China’s clinical trial boom really means for U.S. medicine
